source: Barsalou (2008) Grounded cognition
finding: Grounded cognition says thought uses modal simulation (re-enactment of perceptual, motor and introspective states), bodily states and situated action. It rejects thought as computation on amodal symbols.
numbers: Review of about 28 pages; no single N.
quote: Modal simulations, bodily states, and situated action underlie cognition.
limits: Barsalou warns that the label 'embodied cognition' wrongly suggests everyone claims bodily states are necessary. Mostly descriptive theory.
agent_relevance: Background only: our agent is text-only. The useful idea is that a concept is a re-runnable simulation, not a fixed record.

source: Barsalou (2008) Grounded cognition
finding: Perceptual Symbol Systems (PSS, Barsalou 1999) claims grounded theories can still do symbolic work. Simulators (roughly concepts or types) give type-token binding, inference, productivity, recursion and propositions, using simulation instead of amodal symbols.
numbers: Theory, no numbers.
limits: PSS is a verbal theory; the review says computational implementation is still an open goal. Hard to falsify in general.
agent_relevance: A simulator is like a reusable generator that makes many situation-specific instances. Compare with a schema operator that instantiates a concept per problem.

source: Barsalou (1999) Perceptual symbol systems (abstract only)
finding: Original statement. Association areas capture bottom-up sensory-motor patterns and partly re-activate them top-down as perceptual symbols. Selective attention extracts schematic components; memories of one component organised around a frame form a simulator that yields unlimited simulations. Abstract concepts are grounded in complex simulations of physical and introspective events.
numbers: BBS 22(4):577-660. No numbers in the abstract.
limits: Only the abstract was read this session (full text paywalled); details come from Barsalou 2008. Commentaries in the same issue contested the amodal-free claim.
agent_relevance: Frame plus attention-selected components is a design pattern: concepts as frames filled per situation.

source: Barsalou (2008) Grounded cognition
finding: Lakoff and Johnson (1980, 1999): abstract concepts are understood metaphorically from bodily and situational knowledge (love as eating, happy is up). Key open issue is whether metaphors reflect only linguistic convention or real thought.
numbers: Linguistic evidence across languages; no effect sizes in this review.
limits: Barsalou notes increasing but not conclusive evidence for a thought-level role. Metaphor priming effects are mixed.
agent_relevance: Metaphor mapping could be an analogical operator, but evidence that it improves reasoning is weak. Low priority.

source: Barsalou (2008) Grounded cognition
finding: Property verification: Solomon and Barsalou (2004) found perceptual variables such as property size best predicted verification time and errors; larger properties were harder to verify. Pecher et al. (2003, 2004) found a modality-switching cost when consecutive properties came from different modalities.
numbers: Effect sizes not given in the review; see later lines for original abstracts.
limits: Associative word strategies can masquerade as simulation (see the Solomon and Barsalou abstract line).
agent_relevance: Tests of simulation need controls against word association, which is the same risk for LLM probes.

source: Barsalou (2008) Grounded cognition
finding: Lesion and imaging evidence: damage to visual areas raises loss of animal categories; motor-area damage raises loss of tools. Imaging shows fusiform, temporal and premotor/parietal areas activate for shape/colour, motion and action properties; gustatory cortex activates for foods.
numbers: Review level; cites Martin 2001, 2007, Simmons et al. 2005, 2007.
limits: Correlational activation does not prove necessity. Mahon and Caramazza argue activation may be spread from amodal concepts.
agent_relevance: Shows category-specific grounding. A text agent lacks this but can mimic it with explicit sensory-attribute checklists.

source: Barsalou (2008) Grounded cognition
finding: Barsalou answers the epiphenomenon charge: TMS over motor areas affects language processing, so simulation is claimed to be causal. He says much more research is needed.
numbers: TMS studies cited, no numbers given.
limits: Causal evidence is thin and much of it later contested.
agent_relevance: If simulation is causal then forcing it should help reasoning; for an LLM the analogue is explicit imagery steps, which need direct tests.

source: Glenberg and Kaschak (2002) Grounding language in action
finding: Action-sentence compatibility effect (ACE). People judged sentence sensibility by moving toward or away from the body. Responses were faster when movement matched the implied direction (Close the drawer implies away). The effect held for concrete and abstract transfer sentences (You gave Susan the earring).
numbers: Exp 1: 44 participants, 9 dropped for unstable error rate, leaving 35; interaction F(1,34)=7.75. Exp 2A: N=70, ACE F(1,68)=3.72. Exp 2B: N=72.
limits: Marginal F in Exp 2A. The effect depended on action, not only spatial location of the response. A later multi-lab replication failed (next line).
agent_relevance: Canonical test that language meaning uses motor planning. Not testable on text agents; the lesson is that striking early effects can be fragile.

source: Morey et al. (2022) A pre-registered, multi-lab non-replication of the action-sentence compatibility effect
finding: Eighteen labs ran the ACE with auditory sentences and none found a reliable effect. The meta-analytic estimate was essentially zero.
numbers: Native-English labs: 1,492 recruited, 214 excluded, N=1,278. Average ACE on log lift-off time CI95 [-0.006, 0.004], about plus or minus 0.5 percent. Preregistered negligible range under 100 ms. Original: 155 ms (about 9 percent of 1,766 ms) in Exp 1; 170 ms (about 9 percent) in Exp 2a.
quote: none of the 18 labs involved in the study observed a reliable ACE
limits: Replicated one paradigm version (Borreggine and Kaschak sentences, lift-off latency). Authors say other motor-language evidence (Zwaan and Taylor 2006, Hauk 2004) is not refuted.
agent_relevance: Strong warning: the headline behavioural evidence for motor grounding is not reliable. Treat embodiment effects as unproven when borrowing design ideas.

source: Zwaan and Pecher (2012) Revisiting mental simulation in language comprehension: six replication attempts
finding: Orientation: web replications of Stanfield and Zwaan (2001) found a small match advantage in verifying pictures after sentences implying object orientation.
limits: Median RTs, MTurk, 200 recruited per experiment. Bayes factors show little evidence either way for orientation. VVIQ correlation p=.06 in Exp 1a.
agent_relevance: Even the best-replicated simulation effect is tiny (about 35 to 45 ms). Do not build a scaffold on it.

source: Zwaan and Pecher (2012) Revisiting mental simulation in language comprehension: six replication attempts
finding: Shape: pictures matching the implied shape (e.g. an eagle in the sky versus in the nest) were verified faster. The effect was larger and stronger than for orientation.
numbers: Exp 2a: 57 ms (N=176, p<.001, BF01=0.02); Exp 2b: 70 ms (BF01 about 0.01 to 0.04). Accuracy .98 match vs .96 mismatch (p<.001).
limits: Sentence-picture verification may reflect minimal comprehension or strategy, not full simulation.
agent_relevance: Shape match is the most robust simulation result in this paradigm; implied-property priming is real but small.

source: Zwaan and Pecher (2012) Revisiting mental simulation in language comprehension: six replication attempts
finding: Colour: replications found a MATCH advantage, whereas the original Connell (2007) studies reported a MISMATCH advantage. Direction of the colour effect reversed relative to the originals.
numbers: Exp 3a and 3b, N about 186 and 189 recruited; combined analysis BF01 near .01. Exact per-experiment differences are in Table 1 of the paper and were hard to parse from the PDF text.
limits: Opposite sign to original colour studies; authors say it still supports simulation theory but shows replication matters.
agent_relevance: Direction of an effect can reverse across samples; require a preregistered direction before using an effect as a design signal.

source: Pecher, Zeelenberg, Barsalou (2003) Verifying different-modality properties for concepts produces switching costs
finding: Verifying a property in one modality (BLENDER-loud) was slower after a different modality (CRANBERRIES-tart) than after the same modality (LEAVES-rustling). A second experiment ruled out associative priming.
numbers: Abstract only; no numbers read.
limits: Abstract read through Europe PMC only. Later work (Louwerse and Connell 2011) argued modality-switch costs can come from linguistic co-occurrence statistics.
agent_relevance: Switching costs hint that concepts carry modality tags; an LLM scaffold could tag sub-steps by modality but benefit is untested.

source: Solomon and Barsalou (2004) Perceptual simulation in property verification
finding: Neutral participants showed perceptual effort (property size predicts performance) and instructional equivalence with imagery participants, but only when highly associated false properties blocked a word-association strategy. With unassociated false properties, associative strength predicted verification better.
numbers: Abstract only.
limits: Key boundary condition: conceptual tasks mix simulation and word association; method choice decides the result.
agent_relevance: For LLM tests the same confound exists: statistical association can fake grounded behaviour.

source: Louwerse (2011) Symbol interdependency in symbolic and embodied cognition
finding: Language statistics carry much perceptual information. Embodiment findings attributed to perceptual simulation can be explained by distributional linguistic information (symbol interdependency hypothesis).
numbers: Abstract only; no numbers read.
limits: Abstract read through Europe PMC only. Argued, not decisive: simulation theorists reply that the statistics are themselves grounded.
agent_relevance: Predicts text-only LLMs should reproduce many embodiment effects. Matches the LLM results below.

source: Mahon and Caramazza (2008) A critical look at the embodied cognition hypothesis and a new proposal for grounding conceptual content
finding: Sensory-motor activation during concept use can be explained by a disembodied view with spreading activation, so the evidence does not force embodiment. Strong embodiment conflicts with neuropsychology. Proposal: grounding by interaction, concepts abstract and symbolic with sensorimotor information instantiating them online.
numbers: Abstract only.
limits: Abstract read through Europe PMC only. Position paper rather than data.
agent_relevance: Supports a hybrid view: abstract concept core plus grounded colouring, close to an LLM with tools.

source: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy: Embodied Cognition
finding: Summarises Barsalou PSS (reactivation of sensory areas, motor part suppressed), Lakoff and Johnson (basic concepts like up from bodily experience), and critiques: Mahon and Caramazza (motor activity reflects conceptions, not concepts), Rey (concept versus conception), and open problems with abstract concepts such as justice.
numbers: Martin and Schwartz (2005): children computed one quarter of 8 more successfully when manipulating pie pieces (figures not given in the part read).
limits: Read the first 100,000 of 114,500 characters via a summariser, not raw text.
agent_relevance: Useful map of objections; abstract concepts are the weak spot for pure grounding.

source: Hauk, Johnsrude, Pulvermuller (2004) Somatotopic representation of action words in human motor and premotor cortex
finding: Reading action words (lick, pick, kick) activated motor-strip areas adjacent to or overlapping those for real tongue, finger and foot movement.
numbers: Event-related fMRI, passive reading; numbers not read.
limits: Abstract only. Passive activation could be spread rather than constitutive (Mahon and Caramazza).
agent_relevance: Neural evidence of grounding of action words; background only for a text agent.

source: Binder et al. (2016) Toward a brain-based componential semantic representation
finding: Proposes about 65 experiential attributes (sensory, motor, spatial, temporal, affective, social, cognitive) with salience norms for nouns, verbs and adjectives; the vectors separate a priori categories and capture similarity.
numbers: About 65 attributes; exact word count not read.
limits: Abstract only. Ratings, not behavioural measures.
agent_relevance: A usable checklist of experiential dimensions for a concept-expansion step; LLMs can fill it (see LLM lines).

source: Bisk et al. (2020) Experience grounds language
finding: Argues NLP should climb five world scopes: corpus, internet, perception, embodiment, social. Text-only learning lacks grounding in perception and action.
numbers: Position paper, no experiments.
limits: Later LLM results (Marjieh et al.) show more perceptual structure recoverable from text than the paper expected.
agent_relevance: Frames what text-only agents miss; justifies tools or perception when physical facts matter.

source: Marjieh et al. (2023) Large language models predict human sensory judgments across six modalities
finding: GPT models' pairwise similarity ratings correlate significantly with human ones in all six modalities (pitch, loudness, colours, consonants, taste, timbre) and recover the colour wheel and pitch spiral with octave equivalence.
numbers: Human split-half reliability: pitch r=.90 [.87,.92]; consonants r=.46 [.36,.56]; GPT-4 reported on par with humans there. GPT-4 colour-naming adjusted Rand index English 0.54, Russian 0.54, GPT-3 0.35.
limits: Text-only recovery gives only a lower bound on what language carries; correlation varies by modality; GPT-4 vision training did not specially help colour.
agent_relevance: Text alone carries much perceptual structure. Supports using LLM knowledge for sensory reasoning without grounding.

source: Abdou et al. (2021) Can language models encode perceptual structure without grounding? A case study in color
finding: Text-trained BERT, RoBERTa and ELECTRA show significant representational alignment with CIELAB colour space; warm colours align better than cool colours; alignment is mediated by collocation and syntax.
numbers: 18 colour terms; RSA significant in all setups; permuted centroids give p>0.05.
limits: Small sample (18); mean alignment near zero in some context-free settings.
agent_relevance: Another hint that distributional learning approximates perceptual geometry for colour.

source: Chlapanis, Menis Mastromichalakis, Papadimitriou (2026) The grounding gap: how LLMs anchor the meaning of abstract concepts differently from humans
finding: Replicating human property-generation studies on 21 LLMs: models rely on word associations and underproduce emotion and internal-state properties. In rating tasks LLMs align more closely and improve with size. Sparse-autoencoder features for sensorimotor and social dimensions exist in Gemma.
numbers: 21 models; no model above Pearson r=0.37 with human responses; human-human ceiling above 0.9.
limits: Coding of model outputs was done by an LLM judge (Gemini-2.5-Flash) validated against human-coded labels (human two-coder agreement 76.8 percent and 64.25 percent in the source studies).
agent_relevance: LLMs know grounding categories when asked but do not use them by default. A scaffold step that asks for sensorimotor and affective properties may recruit them.

source: Xu et al. (2025) Large language models without grounding recover non-sensorimotor but not sensorimotor features of human concepts
finding: Across about 4,442 concepts, model-human similarity falls from non-sensorimotor to sensory to motor domains (minimal for motor). Models with visual training match humans better on visual dimensions.
numbers: Glasgow Norms N=829 raters; Lancaster Norms N=3,500; about 4,442 words.
limits: Abstract only. Specific model families compared.
agent_relevance: Motor knowledge is the weak spot of text-only models: use tools or explicit simulation when action detail matters.

source: Oneata, Elliott, Frank (2025) Seeing what tastes good: revisiting multimodal distributional semantics in the billion parameter era
finding: Linear probes on McRae-THINGS norms and Binder attribute ratings: multimodal image encoders slightly beat language-only models, and image-only encoders perform comparably to LLMs even on non-visual attributes. Strong models converge.
numbers: Models include ViT-MAE, DINOv2, CLIP, SigLIP, Gemma-2B, DeBERTa v3; exact scores not extracted.
limits: Concrete concepts only; linear probes; no abstract concepts.
agent_relevance: Vision gives only a small gain on concept attributes; grounding is not a big lever for object knowledge.

source: Wagenmakers et al. (2016) Registered Replication Report: Strack, Martin and Stepper (1988)
finding: Seventeen direct replications of the pen-in-mouth facial feedback study found a funniness-rating difference of 0.03 units, 95% CI [-0.11, 0.16], against 0.82 units in the original.
numbers: 17 labs; original 0.82 on a 10-point scale.
limits: Abstract only. Later work suggests moderators; not checked.
agent_relevance: Bodily-state-to-judgment embodiment effects have a weak track record. Do not import them.

source: Frontiers in Psychology (2025) The action-sentence compatibility effect in third-person action sentence comprehension
finding: New ACE variants claim perspective-dependent effects along front-back and left-right axes depending on animacy and priming.
numbers: Three experiments; N not read.
limits: Abstract only. Published without testing the preregistered null of Morey et al.
agent_relevance: Shows the ACE literature is still active but unresolved.
